This article is a review of task-based functional neuroimaging studies in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome rather than an original fMRI study in healthy adults; it meets the exclusion criterion for reviews (E1).

The article is explicitly a review and meta-analysis of social cognition in PTSD rather than an original fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It meets exclusion criterion E1 (systematic reviews or meta-analyses).

fMRI study where participants evaluated faces varying by race and socioeconomic status (social perception/understanding of others). Sample comprises 61 adult (white male) participants, indicating healthy adult group. Meets criteria I1 and I2 based on abstract information.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of brain responses to faces, voices, and combined emotional expressions—clearly a social perception/understanding of others task. The abstract does not state participant health status or ages (18–65), so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (learning others' trustworthiness) involving healthy younger and older participants. It meets I1 (social-related task during fMRI) and appears to meet I2 (includes a healthy younger adult group likely within 18–65). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI during joint leader–follower interactions (a social-related task) and recruited healthy skilled dancers (adult participants), meeting the review’s focus on social processing in healthy adults. Abstract indicates task-based fMRI and healthy subject groups, so it should be included for full-text review to confirm ages and health details.

The study used resting-state fMRI (rsFC) rather than a task-based fMRI paradigm assessing social-related processing. The review requires functional MRI during a social-related task. Participants are healthy emerging adults (ages ~20–25), so I2 is satisfied but I1 is not.

fMRI study measuring neural representations of others' mental states—clearly a social-related task (Perception and Understanding of Others). Abstract reports human male and female participants but does not specify ages or explicitly state health status, so include for full-text review to confirm criterion I2 (healthy adults 18–65). No exclusion criteria met from abstract.

Study participants are children with NVLD or ASD and typically developing children, not healthy adults aged 18–65, so it fails inclusion criterion I2 (adult healthy sample). The abstract also does not clearly describe task-based fMRI of social processing. Exclude based on participant age/group mismatch.

This is a narrative review of resting-state fMRI findings and manipulations in ASD, not an original fMRI study of social-task performance in healthy adults. It meets the exclusion criterion for systematic reviews/meta-analyses (E1).

Abstract reports fMRI scanning during an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social decision-making task), satisfying I1. The sample (20 male participants) is described but health status and ages are not explicitly stated in the abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone; include for full-text review to confirm participant health/age eligibility.

The study used resting-state fMRI (no task-based social processing) to map a mentalizing network and relies on intraoperative stimulation; it does not report an fMRI scan during a social-related task (fails I1). Participant group appears to be clinical (intraoperative), so healthy adult inclusion is unclear. No systematic review/meta-analysis criteria met.
Study used resting-state fMRI (no social task) and participants are adolescents (mean ~14.5, range 10–18), not healthy adults aged 18–65. Therefore it does not meet I1 or I2.

This article is a multi-method review/meta-analysis synthesizing lesion, TMS, MVPA, and Neurosynth evidence rather than reporting original fMRI scans of healthy adult participants. It meets exclusion criterion E1.

Study used fMRI during a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy subjects randomized to intranasal oxytocin or placebo — meets the review objective. Ages not specified in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm age range (18–65).

Abstract reports neural (amygdala/prefrontal) responses to trust-related interpersonal stimuli in BPD versus controls, implying an fMRI social-processing task and inclusion of a healthy control group. The abstract does not explicitly state scanning parameters or participant ages (18–65), so include for full-text review to confirm methods and age range.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in 93 healthy males performing a Taylor aggression paradigm involving social provocation and decisions about retaliatory behavior (social cognition/perception of others). Participants are healthy adults, satisfying inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes dual-fMRI hyperscanning while pairs performed an interactive social-exchange task, meeting I1. The abstract does not specify participant ages or that they were healthy adults, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify I2.

This is an fMRI study using an interpersonal pleasant touch paradigm addressing social reward/processing, and includes a matched non-using healthy control group of adults. Thus it meets I1 (social-related task with fMRI) and I2 (healthy participants aged 18–65 present). Not a review or meta-analysis.

Study used a sample of early adolescents (ages 10.5–13.4), not adults 18–65, and used resting-state fMRI and MRS rather than a task-based social fMRI paradigm. Thus it does not meet inclusion criteria I1 or I2.
fMRI was conducted during spontaneous conversation and repetition tasks (social-related processing), and the study includes an age-matched typically developing healthy control group (young adults).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI during a theory-of-mind (social cognition) task, satisfying I1. Participants are described as younger and older adults but age ranges are not specified, so it is unclear whether a healthy 18–65 group is present; include for full-text review to confirm I2.
This is an animal study using Fmr1 knockout mice and pharmacological intervention; no human participants or human fMRI social-task data are reported, so it fails inclusion criteria I1 and I2.

fMRI was used to identify and modulate a pSTS region responsive to dynamic facial expressions—a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). The abstract does not state participant health status or ages, so inclusion criterion I2 is unclear; include for full-text review to confirm demographics and health.

The study used task-free (resting-state) fMRI rather than an fMRI social-related task, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I1. Although typically-developing controls are present (I2), the absence of a social task excludes it from this review.

fMRI hyperscanning study of live mutual eye contact—a social interaction task—conducted in human adult pairs. The abstract reports task-related neural activation and connectivity during eye contact, meeting the fMRI social-processing requirement. Participants are described as human adults (healthy sample), satisfying the participant age/health criterion.

fMRI study where participants viewed face images and performed perceptual/recognition tasks—fits social processing domain (Perception/Understanding of Others). Participants are human (male and female); abstract does not state ages/health explicitly, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI during live reciprocal social interactions (human-human vs human-robot), directly addressing social processing and reporting 21 scanned participants. Participant ages/health status are not specified, so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

fMRI was used while participants observed human and robot agents experiencing pain/pleasure, assessing empathy — a social cognitive process. Participants (n=26) were healthy adults. The study meets criteria for social-related fMRI task and includes healthy adult participants. Not a review.

fMRI was used while healthy adult participants watched a narrator using co-speech gestures, addressing social communication and semantic processing in an ecologically valid social interaction. Twenty healthy participants (adults) were tested, satisfying both criteria.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of socioemotional processing (empathy and anxiety), which fits social-related processing (I1). The abstract does not specify participant health status or ages (18–65), so inclusion cannot be confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review to assess I2.

Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based social processing paradigm, so it does not meet I1. Age range is across the lifespan (not specified as 18–65), so I2 is not clearly satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E1) apply.

fMRI study using the Cyberball paradigm (social inclusion) satisfies social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy control group (17 HC) alongside clinical groups; participants appear to be adults. Thus I1 and I2 are met based on the abstract.

The study reports fMRI BOLD responses to animacy perception—a basic social-perception process—so it addresses social-related processing (I1). The abstract does not specify participant ages or explicitly state they were healthy adults, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify eligibility.
This article is a meta-analysis of fMRI studies (not an original fMRI study of participants), meeting the exclusion criterion for systematic reviews/meta-analyses.

The study used resting-state fMRI (connectivity at rest) rather than a task-based fMRI during performance of a social-related task, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I1. Participants appear to be healthy adults (N=50).
Participants are children with ASD and age-matched typically developing children (not adults). No group of healthy adults (age 18–65) is included, so study fails inclusion criterion I2.

The study used fMRI while participants played a virtual ball-tossing game inducing social exclusion (a social-related task) and reports neural correlates modulated by social support. The sample comprises 71 healthy female participants. Thus it satisfies I1 (fMRI during a social task) and I2 (healthy participant group).

The study reports fMRI data including social perception and reasoning tasks (social-related processing) performed by 78 individuals, indicating relevant task-based fMRI in humans. No clinical populations are reported, implying healthy adult participants.

fMRI study investigating processing of dynamic facial expressions (social communication/perception) in a participant sample (n=51). Abstract indicates a social-related task and likely healthy adult participants; age range not reported, so full text review is needed to confirm I2. No exclusion criteria met.

fMRI study investigating neural processing of social (dyadic) interactions, satisfying I1. Abstract does not specify participant age range or explicit statement that participants were healthy adults (I2 unclear). Given insufficient participant detail, include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract reports an fMRI experiment (N=31) measuring neural responses to disfigured faces—a social perception task (perception/understanding of others). It likely used healthy adult participants, though ages/health not explicitly stated; include for full-text confirmation.

fMRI study using vocal emotional stimuli (social communication/perception) with 36 healthy participants; meets criteria of performing a social-related task (vocal emotion processing) and including healthy adults. Age range not specified in abstract, so included for full-text review.

The abstract describes a review of human neuroimaging literature and theoretical discussion of cerebellar function rather than reporting an original fMRI experiment in healthy adults. It is therefore a review article and meets exclusion criterion E1.

The study used resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) before/after rTMS rather than an fMRI task assessing social-related processing, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I1. Healthy adult participants are included (I2).

The study used resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based social fMRI paradigm, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I1 (fMRI during a social-related task). Although healthy controls were included (I2), the primary imaging was resting-state, so exclude for the review focused on task-based social processing.

The study used rtfMRI neurofeedback for hippocampal self-regulation in healthy volunteers, not a social-related task or paradigm probing social cognition/interaction. Although participants are healthy adults (I2 satisfied), the abstract does not describe any social processing task (I1 not met). No exclusion criteria (e.g., E1) apply.

The study used EEG-fMRI during a color discrimination (visual) task and investigates visual gamma and related networks — not social processing. It does not address social-related constructs (I1 not met). Participants appear healthy but lack of social task means it is irrelevant to the review objective.

The study used fMRI during a social trust task (meets I1) but the healthy control group were adolescents aged 13–19, so they do not meet the required healthy adult age range (18–65) specified in I2. Therefore it should be excluded.

The abstract describes a review/meta-analytic study (combining PubMed literature search, Neurosynth meta-analytic database, and resting-state connectivity analyses) rather than reporting new primary fMRI data from participants. This meets exclusion criterion E1 (systematic review or meta-analysis).

The study used fMRI while participants played the prisoners' dilemma (a social/interpersonal decision-making task), and included a healthy control group alongside patients. Thus it satisfies I1 (task during fMRI is social) and I2 (healthy adults included). Not a review article.

Participants are adolescents (age 16–17); inclusion criterion I2 requires at least one group of healthy adults (18–65). Although the fMRI task addresses social-related processing (I1 met), the sample does not include adults, so the study is excluded.

Abstract describes an fMRI study of emotional facial expression processing (a social task), satisfying I1. The abstract does not state whether healthy adult control participants (I2) were included, so inclusion requires full-text review.

The study used resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based fMRI social-processing paradigm. Although behavioral measures of social cognition (emotion/sarcasm recognition) were assessed and a healthy control group was included (I2), the absence of an fMRI social-related task means it does not meet I1.

Abstract reports an fMRI study probing honesty-based trustworthiness impressions and predicting trust behavior, meeting I1. Participant health status and ages (I2) are not specified in the abstract, so inclusion cannot be fully confirmed from abstract alone. Include for full-text review to verify that at least one group are healthy adults (18–65).

The study included only participants with alcohol use disorder (no healthy control group). Inclusion criterion I2 requires at least one group of healthy participants aged 18–65. Although it uses fMRI with emotional face processing (I1), lack of a healthy sample excludes it from the review.

Functional MRI was used while participants observed and discriminated others' hand actions (perception/understanding of others — a social process). The study includes a healthy adult group (n=31). Not a review/meta-analysis. Abstract provides sufficient info to meet inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports fMRI during auditory (voice) stimulation addressing voice processing and social cognition, meeting I1. Participant health/age not specified in abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review to verify participant characteristics.

Study uses multi-voxel pattern analysis of neural representations of social touch (implies fMRI) addressing social processing. Abstract does not clearly state whether a healthy adult control group (age 18–65) was included, so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Abstract reports resting-state fMRI in toddlers with autism (ASD) and an ASD subtype identified by eye-tracking. No task-based social fMRI and participants are not healthy adults (18–65). Does not meet inclusion criteria I1 or I2.

fMRI was used while participants recalled museum displays, and the study addresses collective memory and medial prefrontal cortex involvement in social cognition—meeting I1. The abstract does not specify participant ages or clearly state they are healthy adults (18–65), so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify participant characteristics.

Abstract clearly states this article is a literature review of hallucinogens and entactogens on social processing; it is a review article, meeting exclusion criterion E1 (systematic reviews or meta-analyses). No original fMRI experimental data are described in the abstract.

This study is about developmental and sleep questionnaires for ASD screening in children/toddlers and does not report any fMRI data or involve healthy adult participants (age 18–65). It does not meet the review’s fMRI or adult healthy participant criteria.

This is a machine-learning methods paper on probabilistic graphical modeling for multi-view bipartite graph clustering. The abstract does not describe any fMRI data, human participants, or social-related tasks, so it does not meet the review inclusion criteria.

fulltext_screening_results.reason: This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 24–37; N=10 for fMRI) using socially relevant non-verbal vocalizations and animated faces, addressing social-related perception/understanding of others. Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-by-voxel two-tailed t tests, maps transformed to Talairach space, thresholded maps and ROI analyses) are presented as group activation maps (figures/tables), satisfying group whole-brain voxelwise reporting (not merely ROI-based). Healthy adult results are reported separately and clearly. Although slice coverage was focused on temporal cortex, the paper presents group voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts for the healthy sample, meeting the review’s requirements.

This is an fMRI study of prosody perception and production tied to social communication and empathy (social-related processing). Sample: 19 healthy, right-handed native-English adults aged 18–58 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., “happy-neutral”, “question-neutral”) thresholded and corrected (p<0.05 FDR, cluster k>5) and describes coordinates and supplementary materials; overlap/SVC and whole-brain contrasts are reported in text and figures. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, mean age 25.7) that used a social-emotion task (guilt memories and hypothetical social scenarios) relevant to social cognition/perception of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (thresholded whole-brain maps at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reported activated regions and coordinates) as well as SVC results. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI (task-based) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~31) that uses the Ultimatum Game, a social economic exchange task probing social decision-making and cooperation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunction analyses, whole-brain parametric regressions) with coordinates and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy participant groups. Methods and results provide whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI during social tasks in healthy adults (theory-of-mind and social attribution-of-attention) and meets I3 and I4. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map for the healthy group. Task-related analyses were performed using localized ICA within a TPJ ROI (ROI-limited task decomposition) and task relevance was assessed via IC time-course regressions; whole-brain results are limited to seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting and meets exclusion criteria E2 and E3.

The study uses task fMRI during a social-related face encoding/recognition paradigm (meets I3) and includes healthy adult participants (young subgroup aged 20–31; meets I4). However, the imaging analyses reported are region-of-interest (amygdala) extractions and parameter estimates; the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain results for the healthy group. Because no unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy group is provided, the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore must be excluded under exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using an explicit social task (imitate/observe emotional faces) probing perception/understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group-level analyses (PLS and GLM) with voxelwise brain maps rendered in MNI space and thresholded voxel patterns reported, satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Healthy participant results are reported for the group (neuroimaging data from 20 participants used for final analysis). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level task activation data.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (kinship/ moral dilemma) in healthy adults. It used whole-brain, task-based fMRI during an ecologically valid movie-viewing social/moral task and a separate moral-decision task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of clusters and coordinates (and unthresholded maps referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The study is an fMRI task of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript reports group-level results that were small-volume corrected within a predefined vACC ROI and presents ROI-restricted activation clusters. There is no clear report of an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain task-evoked results, it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (E2).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) that used an active task (viewing erotic pictures and videos of other people) engaging perception of others and reward-related/social-affiliative processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (within-group male vs female stimulus contrasts for each orientation group) with corrected thresholds (p<0.05 FWE) and cluster reports, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criterion (ROI-only, resting-state-only, age outside range, non-empirical) is violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (ages 18–34). The tasks are social-related (perception/understanding of others) and functional MRI was used. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and whole-brain analyses described in the text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognition task (modified Empathic Accuracy Task) that involves perception and understanding of others’ emotions. The sample comprises healthy adults (final fMRI sample N=34, ages 20–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects paired t-tests, TFCE FWE-corrected results) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI whole-brain task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, combined N=59) performing social-related semantic tasks (person knowledge, socially relevant words), satisfying the review’s social-processing target. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., social > non-social semantics) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and peak coordinates presented, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control participants; ROI analyses are supplementary. Study 2 includes control participants reported separately from patient data. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance task contrasting social vs nonsocial stimuli (relevant to social processing constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35, N=76 analyzed) within the 18–65 range; (3) The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes exploratory whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses (with reference to whole-brain results reported in the manuscript/supplement); (4) Whole-brain results are acceptable to be in supplementary materials per criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activation maps). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation of faces varying by race and status) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). The task is clearly social (impression formation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate PLS results (brain–behavior LVs) and displays/thresholds whole-brain voxel maps and cluster reports; GLM preprocessing and contrast images were used as input for PLS, providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of interactive joint-action (leading vs following) that probes social cognitive processes (mentalizing, perception of others) during a social task. Participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean ages ~40) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Leading>Following, Following>Leading, conjunctions) with Talairach coordinates and figures, and whole-brain regression analyses; results are presented for the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social perception (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified for the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain analyses appear to be across all participants or focus on group contrasts (BPD vs controls) and ROI analyses for the amygdala are reported for controls. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a clear, group-level whole-brain healthy/control task map; that requirement is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts or pooled analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults. The task is explicitly social (mutual gaze/eye-blink entrainment) and uses functional MRI (hyperscanning fMRI) with task conditions (LIVE vs REPLAY). The sample is healthy adults (final analyzed N=30 participants; mean age ~21.7 years), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and GLM results in the text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a socioemotional Face Processing Task (fearful vs neutral faces) during functional MRI, addressing social-related processing (I3). The sample comprises 49 healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) with results reported for this healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (F > N, N > F) using whole-brain TFCE/FWE-corrected analyses, including coordinates, figures, and descriptions in the text (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (cyberball) probing social exclusion/affiliation processes in healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates (including clusters surviving FWE small-volume correction) and provides coordinate tables and described contrasts for the healthy/control sample. All required inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in healthy adults are met, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (visual processing of dyadic interactions), using healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain preprocessing and GLM estimation to generate run-wise whole-brain beta maps and report group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests) and whole-brain searchlight analyses. Results include group-level voxelwise classification/searchlight findings and discussion of whole-brain effects. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses/maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or resting-state-only) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social-perception task (gender judgments while viewing faces differing by facial disfigurement) that probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, stigma/dehumanization). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM nonparametric whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and report significant whole-brain activations and deactivations for the healthy sample (figures/tables and ROI/item-wise follow-ups are provided). Thus the paper meets the fMRI social-processing objective, includes a healthy adult sample, and reports unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social neuroeconomic task (prisoners' dilemma) probing social behaviour and cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; ages 18–50) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses for the control group (one-sample t-tests and per-group analyses with whole-brain results described and visualized; thresholding and cluster reporting are provided), satisfying the requirement for unmasked healthy-group whole-brain activation maps. Constructs assessed (trust/cooperation, mentalizing, face trustworthiness) fall within social-related processing. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) apply. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for this review.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (dynamic facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group (TD). The reported whole-brain analyses focus on between-group comparisons and found no significant additional activations; the main task results are given as ROI/MANCOVA analyses and DCM (effective connectivity). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (I5) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This paper reports task-based functional MRI of action observation and weight-discrimination tasks probing perception/understanding of others (social perception). Healthy adult participants are included (multiple experiments with n=79 healthy participants; controls for the SCA6 patient study are reported separately), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve) are reported and described in the text, figures, and supplementary materials. Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical methods. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24) that used task-based paradigms probing social perception (selective attention to eye gaze and identity; passive viewing of direct vs averted gaze). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and statistical contrasts (face vs control; region clusters identified with z>4 and Talairach coordinates via SPM), presented in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and sufficient for screening.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion I3 is satisfied: this is an fMRI study of a social task (racial ingroup/outgroup face perception). Inclusion I5 (reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the provided text: the abstract describes amygdala BOLD differences and an ROI-based analysis but does not clearly report unmasked whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–65) is not verifiable because no ages or explicit healthy adult status are reported in the excerpt. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending the full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied given the incomplete text. Recommend obtaining the complete article to reassess inclusion.

The abstract indicates an fMRI study of social judgments (empathy, forgivability), so I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is satisfied. However the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata), so key eligibility items cannot be verified: participant ages and health status are not reported in the supplied content (I4 not confirmable) and the paper’s reporting of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone (I5 not confirmable). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on available content, but because required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending a complete full text. Full text incomplete flag set.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of social judgment (trustworthiness of faces), meeting the review objective. It tests perception/understanding of others using an explicit/implicit trustworthiness task and reports behavioral and neuroimaging results. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=14, ages 18–30) with group-level random-effects analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise statistical parametric maps and group contrasts (main effect of trustworthiness, task effects, interactions) are reported with coordinate tables and figures; small-volume corrections are applied for ROIs but whole-brain/unmasked results and thresholds are described. The full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-cognitive attribution (perception/understanding of self and others) using task-based fMRI. Participants: 12 healthy adults (ages 20–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects, voxelwise thresholding, tables of coordinates and figures) for contrasts of interest (internal vs external attributions; self-serving vs non-self-serving), with results presented in tables/figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects, participants within age range, empirical study with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/figures described).

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults using a social-interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) to manipulate perceived cooperativeness and intentionality. The scanned sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 25.6, range 21–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with contrasts and tables of peak coordinates and discusses activations in a priori ROIs and whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, paradigm, image acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and neuroimaging, tables/figures), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis eligibility for inclusion as an fMRI whole-brain study of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans (N=13, mean age 27.2) in which subjects passively viewed realistic video clips of social interactions (social-related processing). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (ANOVA, voxelwise P ≤ 0.05 corrected) with figures and a table of activated clusters for contrasts (relational vs. alone; relational vs. rest), clearly from the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social gaze processing (mutual vs. averted gaze) in healthy adult participants. The methods report task-based BOLD fMRI, behavioral validation, and both ROI and voxelwise (whole-brain) group-level analyses, including group-averaged t-statistic activation maps displayed on a standard brain. The sample comprises healthy young adults (reported as ‘healthy young adults’), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps are explicitly described and visualized, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI task probing social processing (cooperation vs. competition) with healthy adult participants (ages 21–28). The full text includes methods, participant info, task design, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts (e.g., cooperation vs. independent; competition vs. independent), with thresholding and tables/figures described. Whole-brain results are reported and described for the healthy sample. The article is an empirical fMRI study (NeuroImage 2004) with complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper). Therefore I include this study for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment), with healthy adult participants (N=19, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (G−N, E−N) using random-effects analyses, tables of coordinates, figures, and thresholding procedures. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

Full text provided is incomplete (only abstract and metadata). While the abstract indicates fMRI experiments addressing theory-of-mind/social interaction (satisfying I3), the paper lacks accessible methods, participant details, and whole-brain result reporting needed to confirm eligibility. I cannot verify that a healthy adult sample (I4) was used, nor that at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available content, but inability to confirm required inclusion criteria and the incomplete full text necessitate exclusion at this stage. Recommend obtaining the full article (PDF) to reassess.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate a social-related construct (perception/understanding of self via self-face recognition), includes healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 26.9, ages within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self>other and other>self) with cluster-thresholding and coordinates in tables/figures. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age sample, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation) in healthy adults (n=14, ages 18.3–23.7), using task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types; impression > sequencing) with statistical thresholds (P<0.001) and MNI coordinates/tables and figures, clearly from the healthy control group. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This paper reports an event-related BOLD fMRI study of self-face versus familiar and unfamiliar faces, which directly addresses social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=12; mean age ~19), and results are presented as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM contrasts: unknown vs scrambled, familiar vs unknown, self vs familiar) with tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.4) that investigates processing of angry prosody—a social-communication/emotion task—meeting the review objective. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates (e.g., STS, amygdala, OFC), clearly identified as healthy/control group results. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (theory of mind and empathy cartoons) in healthy adult participants (n=13; ages 19–36). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2) with reported thresholding and tables/figures of activation foci and conjunction/contrast results, clearly from the healthy/control group. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-related processing (gaze, social communication, perception of self/others) using virtual characters. Participants were healthy adults (n=18, mean age 25.9; analyses reported for n=17), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with contrasts, coordinate tables, SPM maps, ROI masking reported but not limited to ROIs. Whole-brain results are clearly described (MNI/Talairach coordinates, statistical thresholds). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (age 20–28) that explicitly examines perception/understanding of self vs other (detection of visual feedback ownership), which falls under social-related constructs. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and coordinates (tables/figures), analyzed with SPM2, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–32). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with statistically thresholded contrasts and Talairach coordinates (Tables and coordinates provided for group contrasts), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The sample consists of healthy adults and results are reported for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only summary/abstract and metadata provided). Inclusion I3 (fMRI during social-related task: face perception) is satisfied based on the summary. However key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed: I4 (participant sample details/healthy adults 18–65) not reported in provided content, and I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for healthy group) cannot be verified from the summary alone. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available content; the study appears empirical. Because the provided full text is incomplete and critical criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending complete full text.

This fMRI study used an interactive social task provoking reactive aggression (social interaction, perception/understanding of others, empathy). Participants were healthy adult males (mean age 28.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects t-statistics, thresholding, and MNI coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants viewed photographs of social groups and made affective/social judgments (SCM emotions), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants were healthy adults (Princeton undergraduates; mean age 19.5; Study 1: n=10; Study 2: n=12), meeting the sample inclusion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, Talairach normalization), with coordinates, t-values, and contrast maps (e.g., subtractive analyses and 3-versus-1 contrasts) for the healthy participant group. Results are reported as whole-brain group effects in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-related processing (judgments of social concepts). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (categorical subtractions and conjunction analyses) with coordinates and thresholding described, and results are clearly attributable to the healthy participant group (n=26, mean age 29.4). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, fMRI paradigm, image acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for core content.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social perception (facial emotion recognition vs age judgment), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises 29 healthy adult participants (ages 20–35), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (FWE-corrected thresholds), with tables of coordinates and figures showing group activation maps for the healthy sample (explicit and implicit conditions), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment targeting social cognition (self-referential processing and perspective taking), satisfying I3. Participants are described as a healthy sample (no clinical groups reported), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level activations in specific MPFC regions (ventral/dorsal anterior MPFC, posterior dorsal MPFC, left dorsal MPFC), which indicates whole-brain task-evoked group effects consistent with I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. However, the provided content appears to be an abstract-like excerpt rather than the full article (methods, full participant demographics, and full statistical reporting are not included), so fulltext_incomplete=true and certainty is moderate. Inclusion is recommended but verification against the full article (to confirm participant ages and explicit whole-brain voxelwise maps/thresholding) is advised.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (communicative speech production) in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–24). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses and task contrasts (communication vs description; familiar vs unfamiliar) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and provides tables/figures of activated regions. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=28, mean age 22.6) using a social interaction simulation task (socially relevant constructs: affiliation/attachment, perception of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected maps and cluster-corrected interaction effects; tables/figures described) from the healthy sample. All inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain task effects, age within 18–65). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is not accessible; only abstract and metadata are available. However, key items required for inclusion cannot be verified: participant ages and confirmation they are adults 18–65 (I4) are not provided, and the paper PDF (methods/results/tables) is unavailable, so I cannot confirm reporting of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on available information. Because the full text is incomplete and necessary inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending access to the full article.

The abstract reports event-related fMRI in a task of perceiving others' emotional facial expressions (a social-related process), in 14 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 29±6) satisfying the sample criterion. The abstract states that statistical parametric mapping showed activation in dorsal medial frontal cortex, implying a group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis. However, only the abstract/metadata are provided here (no full methods, results tables, or figures), so the full text is incomplete and key details (e.g., explicit statement of whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, coordinates/tables) cannot be independently verified. Inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), and I5 (whole-brain evidence implied by SPM statement) appear to be met based on the abstract. No exclusion criteria are apparent from the available content. Recommend obtaining the complete full text to confirm voxelwise whole-brain reporting and group-level maps.

The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary rather than the full article (fulltext_incomplete=true). While the study clearly uses fMRI during a social-related task (I3 met), crucial information is missing: participant demographics/ages are not reported here so I4 cannot be confirmed, and the text does not explicitly present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinates clearly identified as from a healthy/control group, so I5 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly triggered by the abstract alone, but because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the truncated/fulltext-incomplete content, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This study uses task-based fMRI on social cognition (theory-of-mind: cooperation, deception), includes a healthy adult sample (n=13, ages 22–38), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise contrasts, coordinates, and figures. Results are presented as second-level random-effects contrasts (ToM vs non-ToM and direct condition contrasts) with tables of peak coordinates and rendered activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, participants, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, statistical analysis, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This empirical fMRI study investigates social hierarchy processing using social tasks (stable and unstable hierarchies) — a clear social-related task. Participants were healthy adults within the 18–65 range (mean ages reported, ages 19–43), with N=24 per social experiment. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and statistical thresholds (FDR-corrected) with coordinates and tables/figures (e.g., Tables 1–3, Figures 2–5), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced but core article content is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none.

This is an fMRI study of self/mother referential processing and an abstract social attribution task in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (composite t-maps, FDR-corrected peaks) and tables of coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain reporting. Sample comprises healthy adult participants recruited from a university community (final N=17, mean age 21.5), meeting the 18–65 adult criterion. Tasks are social-related (self/other processing, theory-of-mind/social attribution). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is an fMRI study using a social interactive task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) vs a non-social control (Gamble), addressing social cognition and in-group/out-group processing. Participants are healthy adults (Experiments: n=20 females, mean age 20.8; n=30 mixed sex, mean age 21.2), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (PD–Gamble; in-group–out-group) using random-effects analyses with thresholding and tables of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting (tables/figures and text). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary figures referenced but not required. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self and other recognition), in healthy adult participants (N=35, ages 18–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects, voxel- and cluster-level thresholds) and provides coordinates/tables and figures of task-evoked activation maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of empathy (social-related processing) using SELF/OTHER emotional attribution tasks in healthy adult participants (n=26, ages ~24). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (e.g., SELF- and OTHER- versus high-level baseline) with FWE-corrected whole-brain maps and tables of coordinates, and also reports correlations across the healthy sample. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This full text reports an fMRI study of social processing (social motor response learning/Cyberball-like task) in healthy adults. It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-group t tests) with FDR whole-brain correction and reports coordinates/figures of activations. Sample: 18 healthy adults, mean age 42 ±12 (within 18–65). The social task and Pavlovian task TD-model results are described in introduction, methods, results, and discussion; the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI during a social communication task (gaze following vs finger pointing); (I4) includes a healthy adult sample (n=17, ages 20–34) with results reported for the healthy group; (I5) reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (gaze following vs baseline, finger pointing vs baseline, and subtraction contrasts) with statistical thresholds and cluster reporting; (I6) whole-brain results are described in text and shown in figures/co-ordinates. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Figures, and References).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that explicitly investigates perception/recognition of one’s own versus others’ body parts (a social-related construct: Perception and Understanding of Self/Others). Participants were healthy adults (two samples: N=12 and N=15), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts used to localize EBA, LOC, and early visual cortex (e.g., body > objects, objects > body), provides Talairach coordinates and voxel counts for clusters, and presents whole-brain ROI-localization results and contrasts (reported in text/figures/coordinate form), which satisfies the requirement that whole-brain task-evoked results be available (I5/I6). Analyses focus on task-evoked activation rather than only connectivity or patient vs control contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only limitation, no resting-state/connectivity-only focus, not non-empirical, participants are within adult range). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines social-related processing (mental state attribution/intentional stance) using a task manipulating belief about music origin (Composer vs Computer), directly addressing perception/understanding of others. Sample: healthy adults aged 21–31 (n=12 analyzed), satisfying the age and healthy group requirement. Whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses are reported with voxelwise contrasts and tables of coordinates (cluster correction and uncorrected peaks), fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (theory of mind/social exchange) in healthy adults, using task-based fMRI (Wason selection tasks) with group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and reported voxelwise contrasts. The sample includes healthy adults (N=12 analyzed, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain task activation maps and region coordinates/cluster results for story and card contrasts (group-level analyses), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (12 participants, ages 22–37) that used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses to examine social processing (perception/mentalizing about one vs. two walkers). The paper reports whole-brain contrasts, Talairach coordinates, statistical maps, and detailed methods/results/discussion, satisfying the review objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an event-related whole-brain fMRI study (reanalysis) of perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social interaction / social communication), meeting the review’s social-task requirement. Participants: 17 healthy adult males (mean age 25.9), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and local maxima coordinates (SPM results, threshold p=.001 uncorrected, extent threshold 10 voxels) and provide condition contrasts and FIR time-bin analyses — satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging, analysis), Results (tables/figures/coordinates), and Discussion; full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social processing (gaze modulation of observed social vs. individual actions) with a healthy adult sample (N=17, mean age 26). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses and provides voxelwise results (activation maps and tables of coordinates, p<.001 threshold) for main effects and interactions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed animated approaching characters displaying angry or happy expressions (social-related task). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=10; young adults). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds, anatomical coordinates, cluster sizes, figures, and tables—meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, figures/tables, and discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating action observation/mirror system and sensorimotor learning relevant to social cognition (perception/understanding of others). Participants: 20 healthy right-handed adults aged 20–34 (meets age and healthy-sample criterion). Imaging: task-based fMRI with whole-brain, second-level random-effects analyses; results reported using whole-brain corrected thresholds and peak coordinates/tables (conjunctions, contrasts, voxelwise analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants that reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps. The methods and results describe whole-brain random-effects analyses, cluster results with Talairach coordinates, and task contrasts (vegetable preference vs age; SE vs NS actor contrasts) reported in tables and figures. Participants were healthy undergraduates (mean age 20). The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), and I6 (results reported via coordinates/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (behavioral N=10, fMRI N=12; ages 18–41/18–40) using a social task manipulating social context and goal-directedness of gaze shifts. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects second-level ANOVA) and provides whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures of activations (e.g., gaze shift − no movement; incorrect − correct; social − unsocial). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus it meets criteria for (I3) social-related fMRI task, (I4) healthy adult sample, (I5) whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and (I6) acceptable reporting format. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI with social stimuli (face target detection) assessing social-related processing (I3); the sample is healthy adults (N=19, ages 19.3–47.5) meeting the adult age range (I4); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported using mixed-effects FLAME with cluster correction and contrasts (shape targets–novels, face targets–novels, and their comparison) and results provided as figures and MNI coordinates in Table 2 (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Included for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants using a social-related paradigm (dynamic pupillary mirroring and social salience), satisfying the review objective. Sample: 14 healthy adults (mean age 22), within 18–65. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM second-level random-effects analyses; main effects and interactions reported with cluster thresholds and coordinates), and ROI results are also described. Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of self-related social cognition (general and contextual self-judgments). Participants are healthy adults (Japanese and Caucasian-American university students, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects analyses with coordinate tables and ROI analyses; group-level healthy-participant effects and whole-brain contrasts (e.g., general > contextual, interaction contrasts) are clearly reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an explicit emotion recognition task (social communication/perception of others) in a healthy adult sample (21 right-handed males, ages 21–33). The paper provides group-level whole-brain (whole-slab) analyses and presents voxelwise activation results (ANOVA, activation maps, and whole-slab findings reported at p<.001 uncorrected) in addition to ROI analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age in range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/perspective-taking (social cognition) in healthy adults (N=23, ages 19–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., contrasts Pain>No Pain, No Pain: Dissimilar>Similar) with voxelwise thresholds, figures, and tables of activations, and describes preprocessing and SPM analysis methods. Results for the healthy participant group are reported clearly. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (mental state decoding/‘Reading the Mind in the Eyes’), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American, ages 18–27) with group results reported, satisfying I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrasts (e.g., RME − GD; same- vs other-culture contrasts), with tables of activated regions and coordinate listings and SPM results, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range participants only, or non-empirical paper).

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: I3—uses fMRI during a clearly social task (Trust Game probing reciprocity/mentalizing); I4—sample consists of healthy adults (N=18 analyzed, ages 18–22); I5—reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., defect>reciprocate, reciprocity regressions) with MNI coordinates and statistical thresholds; I6—whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables. This is an empirical fMRI study examining attachment-related processing (social/affiliation domain) using masked facial emotion tasks. The sample comprises 51 healthy adult participants (mean age 28.5), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation results (main effects of masked sad and happy faces vs neutral and correlations with attachment avoidance) with coordinates and statistical thresholds described, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are presented as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and participants are within age range). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study examining social-context modulation of empathy for pain (perception/understanding of others), using an event-related task involving social interactions. Sample: 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.4), reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., pain>no pain; social context contrasts; interaction) with tables of coordinates and whole-brain FDR-corrected results and ROI/PPI complementary analyses. Core article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results provided in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates audiovisual integration of non-verbal emotional signals (social communication) using tasks, meeting I3 and I4. However, the analyses are region-of-interest (STS) based: parameter estimates were extracted from predefined measuring points along the STS and statistical tests were performed on these ROIs. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or tables of whole-brain coordinates for the healthy group; results are confined to ROI MPs. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-cognitive processes (direct and reflected self-appraisals), includes a separate healthy adult group (N=12, ages 22.6–30.4) with results reported, and presents whole-brain, unmasked group-level task activation analyses (one-sample t tests and conjunctions vs. rest, whole-brain corrected and thresholded) for the adult group. The task clearly targets perception/understanding of self, a social-related construct. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of methods and whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition (Theory of Mind) task adapted from the Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition (MASC) in healthy adults (n=18, ages 20–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results (contrasts ToM vs PI) with thresholding and cluster information, tables of activations, figures, and complementary T-PICA analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI for social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates social cognition/empathy by presenting social-emotional and social-relation stimuli. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=16 analyzed; mean age ~27.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (EMOT vs NEUT; TWO vs ONE) with statistical maps and peak coordinates (FDR q<0.05, cluster threshold) and includes tables/figures of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self- and other-referential trait judgments) in healthy adults (n=13, mean age 24.2), satisfying the review topic. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts analyzed with SPM5 (e.g., self>syllables, other>syllables, old/same>new), presents statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables, and uses whole-brain inference (thresholds and clusters reported). Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (joint attention/theory of mind) in healthy adult participants (ages 20–31), satisfying I3 and I4.
