The paper includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (body>place, place>body) with figures and a table of activation centers/coordinates, meeting I5 and I6. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample, or lack of healthy-group whole-brain results) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (a social cognition task relating to perception/understanding of others, empathy, and prosocial behavior), with 22 healthy adult participants (ages 19–38). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., whole-brain corrected maps, reported coordinates and contrasts, supplemental tables) showing VMPFC, pSTC, insula, and connectivity results. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical study). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction and joint attention in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with voxelwise results corrected for multiple comparisons and coordinate tables/figures. Samples are healthy adults (final n=16 and n=13; ages 18–29). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=12, mean age 20.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses with coordinates and cluster-level inference (p<.001, cluster thresholds) and presents tables/figures of activation (putamen, caudate, STS, etc.). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full; healthy-group whole-brain task effects are clearly reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of empathy/social attachment (social-related processing) using a task manipulating perspectives (Self, Loved-one, Stranger), satisfying the review objective. Sample: 36 healthy adult participants (mean age 23) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Pain vs. Neutral; direct comparisons across perspectives) with voxel-level FDR correction and tables/coordinates described in text and supplements. Thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using a socio-emotional preference task (Preference vs Gender) that probes social-related processing (social preference/understanding of others). It reports a healthy adult sample (N=21, ages 23–51) meeting the 18–65 criterion. Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and thresholding are reported (second-level random effects, p<0.05 FDR, tables of activation peaks and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only, age-appropriate, and empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=24 analyzed, ages 19–31) that used a social-related task (familiarity judgments involving personally familiar, famous, and unfamiliar faces) probing social cognition (perception/understanding of others, attachment/affiliation, adaptive social responses). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise group-level contrasts with cluster correction and tables/figures of activation (e.g., P1–Cp1, P2–Cp2, P1–F1, repetition suppression contrasts), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/attribution of mind) using passive viewing of sexualized and clothed human targets—satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (male undergraduates, ages within 18–65), and results are reported for the healthy group separately. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain contrasts with voxelwise threshold p<.001 and cluster correction via AlphaSim; tables and figures show whole-brain results), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without a healthy-group map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of gestural social communication (charades) in healthy adults (mean age 27.5; N=18 analyzed). The experiment measured task-evoked BOLD during gesturing and guessing and reports group-level, whole-brain statistical maps (bbGCM differential Granger-causality maps and GLM results) thresholded for multiple comparisons and shown in figures/SI. The task is clearly social (social communication/understanding of others). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of dynamic facial expressions in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported group-level statistical results are presented using region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with small-volume correction (SVC) for a priori masks; the paper does not report unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps. Although coordinates and cluster statistics are reported, these appear tied to ROI/SVC analyses rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 (no clear whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group map) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain results). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/inferring others’ preferences) in healthy adults (n=64, ages 18–26). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (parametric modulation by self–other discrepancy), with coordinates, tables, and figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze (social-related processing) in a sample of healthy adults (ages 21–37). The full text includes methods, behavioral and fMRI results, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (main effects and interactions), thresholding and cluster-level correction, figures and tables of activations. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables and text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI during a social task (Cyberball) and included a healthy adult participant group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group alone. The paper reports whole-brain results for the combined sample (adolescents + adults) and reports interaction results and post-hoc t-tests (and small-volume-corrected findings) for adults, but adult-specific results are not presented as an unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-adult group map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports interactions/post-hoc/ROI/SVC without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants included), I6 (results reported in standard formats/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-adult group map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (making judgments about self, friends, and strangers) in healthy adults (n=98, mean age 20.7, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) and presents whole-brain maps and coordinates (thresholded maps and ROI/whole-brain analyses). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social processes (empathy and sympathy) using task-based fMRI (block design) and reporting whole-brain, group-level contrasts (PCS–NPS; PCO–PCS) with voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures. The sample includes healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (ages up to 40) as part of the healthy participant group. Whole-brain task activation maps are reported for the healthy group (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), meeting the meta-analysis requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

Full text provided appears to be only abstract and references (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study used fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) so I3 is met. However participants are adolescents (developmental sample), not healthy adults 18–65, so I4 is not met and exclusion criterion E5 applies. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for a healthy adult group are reported (I5/I6 not confirmed). Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting the adult-sample criterion and lack of confirmable whole-brain adult results.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 24.8) that uses an identity-discrimination (individuation) task involving faces — a core social stimulus — addressing perception/understanding of others (social cognition). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA, voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures/tables (Figure S1, Table S1) describing task-evoked activation in the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (ROI and whole-brain), and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, healthy adult sample, empirical data). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study investigating social interaction perception using point-light displays (SI vs NSI). Participants: 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4) meeting the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SI - NSI contrast) using random-effects statistics with FDR correction (p<0.05) and lists peak coordinates/clusters (Table 1 and figures). The task is clearly social-related (perception/understanding of others). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of humor processing (a social-cognition-related task involving affect and theory-of-mind aspects) in healthy adults (N=29, mean age 27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Cartoons vs Neutral and parametric modulation of funniness) with detailed results in the text, figures, and supplementary tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of impression formation and violations of social expectations (a social cognition task). Participants are healthy adults (final N=18, ages 19–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) with FDR-corrected results and tables/coordinates (voxelwise activations and ROI analyses are also reported). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. These facts satisfy all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (social vs. solitary context during encoding and recognition), with a healthy adult sample (N=24, ages 18–28) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (SPM5 contrasts, tables, and figures). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Full text is paywalled and only abstract/metadata are available. The abstract indicates an fMRI task using social interaction videos in healthy adult volunteers (satisfies I3 and I4). However I cannot verify whether the paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5) or whether whole-brain results are reported in acceptable form (I6) because methods, results, tables, and figures are not accessible. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on available information, but inability to confirm I5/I6 prevents inclusion per review rules. Full text incomplete (paywalled).

This is an fMRI study using whole-brain, task-evoked analyses of social judgments (allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance) in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 24.2). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (p<0.05 FWE corrected) with coordinates and figures/tables, and results are clearly reported for the healthy control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so assessment is based on complete article content. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial decision-making (family assistance), a social-related task (mentalizing, affiliation/attachment), conducted in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 20.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and figures, and describes whole-brain regression and PPI analyses; thus whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes healthy adults 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task probing perception/understanding of self (self-face recognition via morphing), with healthy adult participants aged 19–24. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and lists significant clusters with MNI coordinates (e.g., MPFC, PCC, precuneus) and thresholding details. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study involves fMRI of observed social interactions and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps (e.g., STS, mPFC, amygdala) based on n=15, satisfying I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures). However, the full text does not report participant demographic details or explicit ages, so I cannot confirm the presence of a healthy adult sample aged 18–65, thus failing I4. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met from the available text. Because core participant information is missing, fulltext_incomplete=true and the study is excluded pending complete reporting of sample age/health status. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: [].

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (eye contact and mimicry) in healthy adults. The study used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Congruent > Catch, interaction contrasts) reported with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (Table 1, figures), and results are clearly from the healthy/control sample (20 right-handed adults, mean age 23). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, DCM connectivity, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task studies with whole-brain healthy-group results.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults that reports group-level task activation contrasts. I3: The task is social-comparative (perception/understanding of others - romantic partner vs. roommate). I4: Sample consists of healthy adults (N=20; mean age 18.7; ages within 18–65). I5: The paper reports second-level (group) random-effects SPM contrasts and voxelwise statistical maps (e.g., Target × Breadth interaction, Valence contrasts) with cluster-level/FWE-corrected results and identified activation peaks (coordinates and statistics). I6: Whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures (coordinates, peak t-stats, cluster sizes). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From abstract, the study is an fMRI investigation of face-voice integration in 20 healthy adults, so inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) appear satisfied. However, I cannot verify I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy group) because the full methods/results are not available. The paper also reports PPI connectivity, but connectivity alone does not satisfy I5 per criteria. Because the required whole-brain healthy-group activation maps cannot be confirmed from the provided text, the study is excluded pending full-text review. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone.

This is an fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing (stereotypes/knowledge of social categories) using task-based fMRI contrasts of social vs non-social categorical judgments. Sample: 19 healthy adults, ages 19–28, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (e.g., ‘social > non-social’ and ‘non-social > social’) with cluster-corrected results presented in figures and tables. Whole-brain results are described in the text and displayed in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages fall within 18–65, and the paper is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study of supramodal emotion perception (socially relevant processing of facial and vocal emotions), which falls squarely under social communication / perception of others (I3). The sample comprises 24 healthy adults aged 18–34 (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts using random-effects GLM and FDR-corrected maps (e.g., CAV > ICAV, AV > A/V) and provides activation tables and figures (I5, I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study using a social competition paradigm (human vs. machine) that explicitly targets Theory of Mind/social interaction processes (social-related processing). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age 35.9), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (main effects and interactions) with tables and figures of activated clusters (thresholds and coordinates provided). Whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (social exclusion via Cyberball), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=20 after exclusions; mean age ~25), satisfying the sample age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (social exclusion > fair play; same- vs other-gender contrasts) with statistical thresholds, cluster correction, tables/figures of activations, and ROI analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures) are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-interaction task (the ultimatum game) to probe social decision-making and predicts accept/reject responses from BOLD data. Participants were healthy adults (male, ages 23–28), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, across-subject multivariate (SVM/RVM) analyses with voxelwise discriminating volumes, MNI coordinates, thresholding (p<0.05) and cluster extents (Tables/Figures), i.e., group-level whole-brain results clearly attributable to the healthy participant sample. Whole-brain results are provided in text/tables/figures (supplementary figures/tables described). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (perception of others' actions/biological motion), with a healthy adult sample (13 right-handed males, mean age 28.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (random-effects analysis, p<0.05 corrected) with coordinates and tables/figures (Table 1, activation maps), and includes methods, results, and discussion in the full text. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines social-related processing (affective/CT-targeted touch) in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–35). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM contrasts (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, and direct arm>palm) with tables/figures and cluster/FDR corrections, and also provides PPI connectivity analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=19, age 18–51) using an explicit social-related task (emotional prosody comprehension — social communication/perception of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotional vs. neutral; complex vs. simple) with cluster-level correction and MNI coordinates, clearly from the healthy/control group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants performing a social-related action-perception task examining in-group/out-group effects. Participants are healthy volunteers (adult majority within 18–65), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (cluster-level PFWE < 0.05 whole-brain corrected) with coordinate tables and descriptions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition using a social working memory task (trait ranking of friends), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 16 healthy adult participants (mean age 20), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric load effects) with coordinates, figures, cluster thresholds, and statistical thresholds described, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; results for the healthy group are clearly reported. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic (social) decision-making—directly addressing social processing (perception/understanding of others). Participants: 32 healthy adult males (mean age 22.8), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLMs, conjunctions, cluster-corrected results) with tables and figures listing whole-brain activation clusters and thresholds. All required core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not outside age range, not non-empirical).

This fMRI study investigates neural responses to communicative vs noncommunicative vocal sounds (a social-communication task) in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22), using whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (vocal > nonvocal; communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded and reported with peak coordinates and figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during social-related task—social communication), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts), and I6 (coordinates and figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete. Therefore I INCLUDE the study for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using BOLD fMRI during a social perception task (viewing affiliation, isolation, and nonsocial images while making pleasantness judgments). It includes a healthy younger adult group (mean age 20.75) within the 18–65 range and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (thresholds, tables of coordinates, conjunctions, and figures). Results for the healthy younger group are reported within the whole-brain analyses. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, and figures) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Visual–Verbal Self-Other Referential Processing Task) examining self- and other-referential processing (social cognition). Sample: 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52 with screening for psychiatric history—meets healthy adult group criterion. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation analyses are reported (SPM8 preprocessing, group contrasts, tables and figures showing whole-brain maps and coordinates), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social evaluation/impression formation (social cognition) using task-based fMRI (I3). The paper includes a healthy young adult group aged 20–29, satisfying the 18–65 age requirement and reporting group-level results for that healthy group (I4). The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses and report corrected cluster results and tables/figures for group effects (I5,I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-only outside range, or non-empirical issues).

This paper reports an fMRI study of impression formation/updating (social perception of others), using a task that is squarely social in content. Participants were healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–45). The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (interaction and L2>F3 contrasts, with voxel-wise thresholds, cluster correction, and supplementary tables/figures), clearly presenting whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete for screening purposes (core sections present).

This is an fMRI study of affective speech comprehension (social cognition/Theory of Mind) in healthy adults (N=51, ages 18–53). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with SPM analyses and FWE-corrected statistical maps and ROI definitions; results are presented as whole-brain maps/tables and discussed for the healthy sample. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy/familiarity/attachment) in healthy adults. The sample is healthy adults (N=22, mean age 23.6), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (threat minus safe), conjunction analyses, whole-brain higher-level comparisons, and tables/figures of coordinates and clusters; results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Full article content including methods, results and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: It uses task-based fMRI during a social-context task (adult expert advice influencing decisions), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45) with results reported for that group, satisfying I4. The manuscript reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (e.g., DLPFC, vmPFC) derived from second-level contrasts, satisfying I5. Whole-brain results are reported in text and coordinates/figures/tables (and supplementary materials), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include healthy adult participants. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using movie viewing of human emotional interactions to probe social-emotional processing, reporting voxelwise, whole-brain intersubject correlation (ISC) maps and ISC-by-valence/arousal GLMs (voxelwise permutation testing and FDR correction). Sample: 16 healthy adults aged 25–49 (within 18–65). Whole-brain group-level results are reported in figures/tables. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=94 females, ages 18–35) that used a social-affective task (Socio-affective Video Task) probing responses to others’ distress (perception/understanding of others, affiliation-related processes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (e.g., HE vs LE videos; parametric modulations of empathy/affect) with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures describing whole-brain effects for the healthy participant group. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study on social cognition (predicting another's choices) using an explicit social “Other” task, satisfying the social-processing scope. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=36 analyzed; recruitment and age range appropriate). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses with corrected p-values and presents tables of activated coordinates (Tables 1 and 2) and whole-brain figures, meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting requirement. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and imaging analyses) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This fMRI study investigates social motivations (affiliation and power) using task-based movie clips in a sample of healthy adult participants (mean age 23.6). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (affiliation>control; power>control) and regression analyses linking individual motive scores to brain activation, with coordinates and cluster results provided. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants (N=27 healthy right-handed adults, ages 24.9–26.3) viewed cooperative and affective social interactions during task fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, full-factorial second-level analyses), thresholded with FWE correction and additional uncorrected maps; results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates. The task probes social-related constructs (perception and understanding of others’ intentions/affiliation). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using naturalistic audiovisual movie clips to probe social perception in healthy adults (n=19, ages 21–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (both non-orthogonalized and orthogonalized regressors), statistical maps (FDR-corrected), and coordinates, clearly attributable to the healthy/control group. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for fMRI social processing in healthy adults. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided in detail. No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task probing affiliative vs nonaffiliative scenarios during task-based fMRI (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age ~27, n=27 analyzed) with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (maternal response to infant cry; attachment/affiliation constructs). Participants are adult mothers (mean age 24.1), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FSL, FLAME, whole-brain FDR .05 threshold) with tables/figures of coordinates and cluster results. Results for the (healthy) adult participant group are reported clearly. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Note: sample includes some high-risk history (perinatal MDE history, 3 on SSRIs) but none met criteria for a current major depressive episode at time of scanning, and analyses considered depressive symptoms as covariates. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an original fMRI experiment on perspective-taking/empathy (social cognition) in healthy adults (n=18, ages 21–31). It uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (first- and second-level SPM analyses, paired t-tests, conjunction, cluster- and peak-level FWE correction) and reports whole-brain activation results (tables and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for a social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and presentation of whole-brain group task-evoked maps/results (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, outside age range, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes social cognition conditions (false-belief/social videos) in a sample of healthy adults (n=45, mean age 20.5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (fixed and random effects), corrected statistical maps, figures, and peak coordinates (Appendix A), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Appendices, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample) are met. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: perception/understanding of others’ emotional facial expressions (meets I3). Sample includes 23 healthy adult human participants (ages 24–34) reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and cluster-corrected random-effects group analyses with coordinates and surface maps (meets I5 and I6). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, coordinates) is provided in the supplied full text (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (action understanding/mentalizing) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32). The methods describe task-based fMRI with group-level random-effects (within-subjects factorial) analyses and reported activation results (conjunctions, F contrasts, cluster-corrected maps) for the healthy participant group. Although main analyses were reported within an a priori mask, the manuscript explicitly states that whole-brain results are provided in the Supplemental Methods (acceptable per I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processing (visual perspective taking/Theory of Mind) in healthy adults. The sample comprises healthy participants aged within 18–65 and results for the healthy group are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8; cluster-level FWE correction) with contrasts and tables/figures of activation (coordinates and cluster-corrected maps). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study in a healthy adult sample (N=21, mean age 24) that investigates neural responses to observed actions and trained shape-action associations (mirror-system/adaptive responses). The task involves perception and understanding of others' actions (a social-related construct). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses including an ROI analysis and a whole-brain analysis (p<0.001 uncorrected) with peak coordinates and tables of results, satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition contrasting interactive vs observational conditions (meets I3). Sample comprised 22 healthy adults (mean 25 yrs), reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level fMRI analyses (two group RFX ANOVAs) and describes whole-brain exploratory results (e.g., V1) and reports voxel coordinates/peak activations alongside ROI SVC analyses—providing group-level task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (meets I5 and I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults, empirical data). Therefore INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study that directly manipulates social vs nonsocial information in an n-back task (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (final imaging N=14, mean age 22; participants recruited from university; meets I4). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA), cluster-corrected maps, and tables of peak coordinates and figures describing the effects (meets I5 and I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and reports unmasked healthy-group task effects, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper should be included in the review.

The study used task-based fMRI while participants viewed others in pain (a social cognition task related to perception/understanding of others), recruited healthy adult participants (N≈36, ages ~21), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinates (whole-brain analyses with FDR correction, tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of methods and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This paper reports original fMRI data using social/person-related tasks (familiar, famous, and novel faces; social closeness judgments) addressing perception and understanding of others. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15 analyzed, mean age 22.33), within the 18–65 range. The authors report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects GLM; voxelwise FDR-corrected maps and cluster-thresholded results) and provide peak coordinates in Talairach space. Whole-brain contrasts relevant to social processing are clearly described (e.g., Facesfamous vs. Facesnovel; Facesfriends vs. Facesnovel), and results are reported in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria appear to be met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical design). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used task-based fMRI to investigate perception of face gender (a social-perception construct: perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–42; N=16, one excluded for motion). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (random-effects GLM, contrast gender-different > gender-same) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and coordinates (Figure and Talairach coordinates). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (final N=17; mean age 23.5) using a social-related task contrasting human vs computer opponents (social resource conflict), satisfying the review topic. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8, second-level random-effects factorial models), thresholded maps, figures, and tables of activation coordinates for contrasts such as Conflict > No-Conflict and interaction effects, clearly derived from the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–27) that used task-based paradigms probing social-cognitive processing (Why-How action identification and Categories-Exemplars), i.e., social-related construal/mentalizing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests; thresholds and cluster correction via Monte Carlo; tables/figures of activations) for relevant contrasts and conjunctions. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines social perception (comparisons of physical attractiveness of people) using a task involving judgments about others’ beauty—a social-related construct (I3). Sample comprises 25 healthy adult women (mean age 23.46), meeting the healthy adult age/sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain thresholds, conjunctions, tables of coordinates, figures) and ROI checks, with results clearly described for the healthy participant group (I5, I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only samples, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (social learning/exclusion using a cyber-ball task) in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 24.1), meeting construct and sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from an exploratory searchlight analysis (random-effects group analysis with family-wise error correction and MNI coordinates reported for STS), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. ROI analyses are also reported but do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range across two experiments (N=25, ages 19–27; N=14, ages 18–23), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts and multivariate searchlight results (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; same>different MVPA) with tables and figures of coordinates and corrected thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/ connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing using a real-world social task (speed-dating) with healthy adult participants (scanned N=38, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Match vs Unrequited; violations of expectation) with tables of coordinates and thresholding details, and includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 24). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction CInt0° > CInt30°) with coordinates, figures, and statistical thresholds, and also reports psychophysiological interaction results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-affiliation/attachment task (hand-holding by friend, stranger, or alone) with threat/safety cues. The sample consists of healthy adults (mean age 23.6). The authors performed group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FLAME cluster-wise thresholding) to identify ROIs and report coordinates and cluster statistics (Table 1) for threat-minus-safe contrasts and handholding interactions. Whole-brain results are clearly reported in the text/tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26), using task-based paradigms manipulating social information (categorization vs. counting). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, second-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CSL>TIC, CAT>COU), cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (imitation/observation of communicative gestures) in healthy adult participants (n=20 reported; mean age 24.6), reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected statistics across multiple contrasts (e.g., IMI>CT, S>NS, interactions). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and all inclusion criteria. It uses functional MRI during a social-related task (compassion/empathy responses to images of human suffering; I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–45 with analyses reported for the healthy groups (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., whole-brain Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC clusters), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5). Whole-brain results are described in the text and supplemental materials (coordinates and corrected clusters), which meets I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, nor restricted to connectivity/resting-state only, nor to participants outside the age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-related processing (playing for self, friend, antagonist) in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (repeated-measures ANOVAs) with voxelwise results, coordinate tables, and figures; small-volume corrections are applied but whole-brain maps and coordinates are presented. Full methods, results, and discussion are included in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural responses during a social communication task (message propagation), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants were healthy adults (interns N=19, producers N=79; mean ages ~20.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (whole-brain thresholding, corrected p-values, MNI coordinates reported in tables/figures) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates perception/understanding of others’ action ‘vitality forms’ (a social-related construct) using a task contrasting attention to action goal (what) vs vitality (how). Participants are healthy adults (n=19, ages ~21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., contrasts how vs what) with reported coordinates, statistical thresholds (PFWE), tables and figures. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment examining social cognition (theory of mind, emotion and pain judgments about others) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=46 females, ages 18–31). It includes group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (one-sample t-tests with whole-brain maps, tables, and figures) and multivoxel pattern analyses reported across the whole brain. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: task-based fMRI of social processes; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results provided in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluation task (being watched by a peer) during fMRI, reporting task-evoked activations and connectivity. The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 8.0–22.9, thus containing adults 18–22.9 within the 18–65 range). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical results (corrected clusters and peak coordinates for MPFC and striatal coupling) and provides coordinates and cluster statistics in the text/supplement. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed dyadic nonverbal interactions and rated naturalness during task-based fMRI. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=21, ages 23–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-level corrected; coordinates and tables/figures provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Full text is present (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation (social perception/understanding of others) using task-based BOLD fMRI (I3). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 19.1) within 18–65 (I4). The manuscript reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts from the healthy sample (e.g., functional localizer contrast form impression > sequencing; cluster-corrected results and Talairach coordinates presented in tables and text), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). Analyses include cluster-corrected maps and coordinates (Tables 1–2) and describe methods for whole-brain GLM and corrections. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range-sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social perception (biological motion) using a passive viewing task—satisfying I3. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult group (n=48; ages 20–35) with results reported separately—satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported for adults (e.g., biological > scrambled motion, Sex × Condition ANOVA) with thresholding, cluster correction, tables of coordinates, and figures—satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the paper does not report only ROI or only connectivity or only between-group contrasts, includes adults within 18–65, and is empirical. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=45, ages 19–28) that uses task-based fMRI to investigate social-signal detection and mental-state inference. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxel-by-voxel regression, cluster correction) with coordinates/figures and tables of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, analyses), Results and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (third-party punishment; mentalizing/attribution of others’ intentions), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages mean 26 within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects multisubject GLM; whole-brain FDR thresholding) and provides peak coordinates and figures describing activations (e.g., R TPJ interaction, R anterior insula main effect). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social stimuli (traffic campaign videos) to probe socio-cognitive processing (STS responses), with healthy adult participants aged 19–30. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (CV vs NV) for each group (Fig. 1) and describes between- and within-group analyses; whole-brain results for the healthy control/safe driver group are clearly presented. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of face processing (a social-perception construct) using a simple viewing task (faces vs objects), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=21, ages 18–37) reported separately in participant tables and ROI statistics. The manuscript performs and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (faces>objects) with results presented in figures and Table 3 (coordinates) and whole-brain maps (regression and contrasts), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are described in the text and tables (acceptable per I6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related attribute framing task (self and reflected perspectives) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 19–41). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (GLM contrasts such as positive minus negative frame, frame-inconsistent minus frame-consistent) with thresholding and peak coordinates described in the Results, satisfying whole-brain group-level reporting. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata/references provided). The abstract shows an fMRI social task evaluating approachability of faces, so inclusion criterion I3 (social-related fMRI task) is met. However, I cannot confirm participant ages and that the reported results are from a healthy adult group (I4) because the full methods/participant section is missing, nor can I verify that the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group (I5/I6). Although the abstract describes activations (e.g., left amygdala) and references SPM and cluster thresholds, without the full text I cannot confirm whole-brain, voxelwise group maps or tabled coordinates. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available content. Because required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the provided incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending access to the full article.

This article reports task-based fMRI studies of social/empathic processing (emotional egocentricity bias) in healthy adult participants, with group-level voxelwise analyses and reported coordinates/tables. Specifically: (1) uses fMRI during a social-related task (empathic judgments; fulfils I3); (2) samples are healthy adult participants (female undergraduates; fulfils I4); (3) reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical contrasts (exploratory whole-brain analysis in fMRI Experiment 1 and group-level contrasts with reported MNI coordinates in fMRI Experiment 2; fulfils I5); (4) results are reported as coordinates/tables and described in text (fulfils I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing using a task (Dynamic Social Gesture) involving social vs. nonsocial gestures, actor-orientation, and face-visibility. The sample is a healthy young adult group (N=20; mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7) and the paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (TFCE with permutation testing) with tables/figures of results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task studies with healthy adults and provides whole-brain activation maps/reports.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=32, mean age ~24.7), using a social incentive force task manipulating collaboration, competition, and individual contexts. The study collected task-evoked BOLD data and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects; clusterwise FWE correction) with figures and a table of activation peaks (ventral basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC, etc.). Behavioral and structural (VBM) results are also reported. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (functional MRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete, containing introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study directly probes social-related processing (judgments of social coordination) in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 23–39). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses are reported (FDR-corrected), with tables and figures describing voxelwise results and coordinate tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study relating grey matter volumes to proneness to moral sentiments using a behavioral task (VMST). It does not report any task-evoked functional MRI whole-brain results from the healthy group. A subgroup (N=29) had prior fMRI data referenced for secondary correlational analyses, but the paper does not present a healthy-group, whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI statistical map required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task) and I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group). The sample meets I4 (healthy adult participants). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI during a social-related task (live verbal communication) in healthy adults (22 right-handed women, mean age ~27), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (talking, listening, imagining) and inter-individual coupling analyses. Whole-brain results are reported with cluster thresholds, figures, and supplementary tables/coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range appropriate, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete.

The article reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness, happiness) using vocal stimuli in a sample of healthy adults (N=44; ages 21–60), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates (conjunctions, contrasts, tables/figures), providing whole-brain task activation maps and coordinate tables (I5,I6). The task is clearly social-related (I3). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social communication/empathy using naturalistic video stimuli (meets I3). Sample comprises 27 healthy adult participants (mean age 34.07), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts and provides coordinate tables/figures of task-evoked activations (satisfies I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only-connectivity-only analyses, no between-group-only contrasts, age within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of social processing (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) in healthy adult participants (n=15, ages 21–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (ANOVA, contrasts), thresholding procedures, cluster extents, coordinates, conjunctions, and figures/tables of activations—i.e., voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results presented in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study of a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (N=35 after losses; mean age 24.6), reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (contrasts and cluster-corrected results) with coordinates and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, and reports whole-brain GLM contrasts clearly from the healthy sample. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This publication is a narrative review article (non-empirical) in Japanese and does not report original fMRI data, participant samples, methods, or group-level whole-brain task activation maps for healthy adults. Exclusion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data) applies. No inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social task) not met, I4 (healthy adult sample reported) not met, I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported) not met. Full text appears to be only abstract/metadata, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This paper reports an fMRI task examining perception/processing of personally familiar faces (partner, child, friend), a social cognition/affiliation-related paradigm relevant to perception and understanding of others (meets I3). It includes a separate healthy control group (13 healthy adults; mean age 64.5 ±5.7) reported separately from the patient (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts from the control group (e.g., partner > unfamiliar; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables/figures), satisfying I5 and I6. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Note: controls are older adults near the upper age bound (mean 64.5) but are a healthy adult group reported separately; therefore included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the ultimatum game (a social decision-making task) and reports task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. It includes a healthy adult group (n=15, ages 19–28) with group-level one-sample t-tests and between-group analyses; results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (free online reciprocal imitation) in healthy adults (N=23 females, ages 18–30). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE), and provides coordinates/tables and figures. It therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=8, ages 22–39) receiving natural interpersonal touch, a social-related stimulus. It reports group-level whole-brain spatial maps (group ICA z-maps thresholded and displayed across the brain) together with task-evoked component time courses and statistical comparisons between stimulus types. Thus it meets inclusion: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), and I5 (group-level whole-brain maps/task-evoked responses). Reporting format is acceptable per I6. The paper is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state-only analyses without task maps, and not a non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I include this study for the review.

This empirical paper reports fMRI data from a faces-versus-houses task in a sample of healthy young adults (mean age 18.87; fMRI subset N=22 after exclusions). The study conducted standard first- and second-level SPM analyses and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activations (significant clusters and a Table 2; figures show FWE-corrected activations). Face perception is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others). Healthy adult results are reported separately (the control/non-clinical sample), satisfying the sample requirement. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Included: The study reports task-based fMRI during social-related trials (social distance: friends vs acquaintances), satisfying the social processing requirement. The sample is healthy adults (N=15; ages 20–28), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and RSA analyses with group statistical maps/clusters and tables (conjunction analyses, FDR-corrected clusters) described in the text and tables, satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Reporting of whole-brain results is explicit (clusters, maps, tables). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes an explicit healthy-group task effect, and is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI of social processing (social closeness judgments) in a sample that includes healthy adults (ages 19–30), satisfying inclusion criteria I3 and I4. However, the fMRI results are analyzed and reported using ROI-based extractions (mean beta weights from predefined anatomical ROIs) rather than reporting any unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self/other/reflected evaluations), includes a healthy adult group (N=19; ages 22–31), and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and cluster results (voxelwise thresholds, AlphaSim correction, tables/figures). Whole-brain analyses and coordinates for effects are provided and results for the healthy adult group are clearly described. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (bystander/emergency observation) using healthy adult participants (aged 18–27). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses and report voxelwise results (parametric effects and contrasts) with cluster-level corrections and tables/figures of activation, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognitive processing (causal attribution/mentalizing) in a healthy adult sample (N=20, ages 18–41). The task is social (self/other/situation attributions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain FWE-corrected results (conjunctions and contrasts versus a truth baseline) and refers to Table 1 and figures with coordinates; whole-brain ANOVA and contrasts are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=50, ages 18–49) investigating social attribution (rating another’s awareness). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (H trials − E trials) thresholded and corrected with coordinates and figures (Table 1, Fig. 3), and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.
