This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=26, mean age 20.7) using social tasks (Cyberball exclusion and a modified Dictator Game) directly addressing social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality) with tables of significant clusters and coordinates and mentions voxel-wise FDR correction for some results, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task contrasts reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (anticipatory active interpersonal touch), involving healthy adult participants (N=16; ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts and cluster-corrected statistical maps (random-effects analyses, Talairach coordinates, tables/figures), not limited to ROI or connectivity-only results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment probing self-/other-referential episodic recollection (a social-cognitive task), satisfying the review topic. Participants were healthy adults (n=18, age 19–29), meeting the sample criterion. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (conjunctions, old>new contrasts) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results reported in tables and text (see Tables 2–3 and whole-brain results described in Results), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and tables, meeting the reporting criterion. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=21 analyzed; mean age 23.1) that used task-based functional MRI during a social/intergroup competitive task involving self- and other-referential moral processing. The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain random-effects analyses (tables and figures provided), including group-level whole-brain contrasts (e.g., localizer self>other; whole-brain analyses collapsing across conditions; Table 1 and Table 2, Supplementary Fig. 1) with corrected thresholds. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating facial color processing, which is directly relevant to social-related processing (social communication / perception of others). It tested healthy adult participants (25 adults, mean age 25.24) so sample meets age/group requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (natural-colored face vs natural-colored scrambled image) with figures and coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Whole article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical).

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social feedback processing (self/other trait ratings) in healthy adult German and Chinese participants, satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are adults (healthy, 18–65), and behavioral and fMRI methods, results, and discussion are fully described. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (e.g., whole-brain and small-volume corrected contrasts with FWE-corrected clusters, tables of activations/coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is present. No exclusion criteria were met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is included for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment involving a social interactive task (interactive rating with an interaction partner) addressing social appraisal/conformity (satisfies social-related processing). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=20 scanner participants; mean age ~24) reported. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects, clusterwise FWE correction over the entire brain; tables and figures of activations provided). Results are reported for the healthy/control group (no clinical groups confounding). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing using first-person video clips of social interactions (reactive–aggressive, social-positive, neutral), satisfying the review objective. Sample: 20 healthy adult males (mean age 24.6), meeting the healthy adult sample requirement. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported (second-level random effects analyses, p<.05 FDR-corrected, k≥5) with tables of peak coordinates and conjunction analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy group. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social processing (perception/understanding of others) in healthy adults. Ten healthy male adults (ages 22–32) were scanned while viewing social point-light displays; the paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (atypical vs typical) with voxelwise maps, cluster correction, tables of coordinates, and connectivity analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (imagined triadic interactions) in healthy adults, meeting the meta-analysis objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: triadic, self-, other-referential processing), I4 (sample: 19 healthy adults age 18–35, group results reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported with thresholds p<0.05 FWE and contrasts such as triad>iron, conjunction analyses; coordinates/tables provided), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=28, mean age 25) that used a social decision-making task (Ultimatum Game) during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts and clusterwise-corrected results (e.g., fairness main effects, interactions, and [high(unfair−fair) − low(unfair−fair)] contrasts), with coordinates and figures/tables described in the text. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (an fMRI-adapted Taylor Aggression Paradigm with videos of an opponent showing angry vs. neutral expressions), conducted in healthy adult participants (32 analyzed, mean age 23.3). The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., angry > neutral) with cluster-wise FWE correction and provides tables/figures of these group-level voxelwise results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (matching-pennies game with human and non-human agents) that probes social cognition/mentalizing. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=16; ages 18–25) reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM results are reported (voxel-wise threshold p<.001 with cluster-level FWE correction) with region coordinates and figures/tables (Tables 2–3; Fig. 6), clearly from the healthy group. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete and open access. Therefore it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed an impression-formation task (social evaluation of others varying in moral and financial status) during task-based fMRI. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult males (ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain ANOVA, thresholded maps and Table 1 with coordinates) in addition to ROI results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (implicit false-belief/theory-of-mind) in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.7). It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM contrasts (false-belief > false-photo/map) with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates reported, and describes an explicit whole-brain localizer and subsequent whole-brain analyses for the implicit task. Sample size and results are reported for the healthy group separately (behavioral n=18, MRI n=16). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The provided document includes abstract and highlights indicating an fMRI study of interpersonal synchrony (N=100) with behavioral and neuroimaging findings, which supports inclusion criteria I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants). However, the full text is incomplete: only abstract/metadata are present and key sections (detailed methods, results, group-level whole-brain statistical maps or coordinate tables) are missing. Therefore I5 (reporting at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met based on the available content. Decision: EXCLUDED pending access to the complete full text that confirms I5.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (empathy induction via traffic-awareness campaign videos), includes a healthy adult sample (20 males, ages 20–28), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (CV > NV) with FWE-corrected results summarized in tables/figures. Behavioral measures and ROI follow-ups are also reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper’s reported significant results are presented with ROI-based (small-volume/FWE-corrected) analyses and PPI connectivity results; the authors explicitly state there were no significant whole-brain effects at P<0.05 FWE without the covariate. The manuscript does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain significant activation table for the healthy group. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting (I5) and falls into exclusion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E2. Full text appears complete.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using perception of biological motion (a social-related stimulus), with a healthy adult sample aged 18–39. The authors conducted and reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain analyses of biological-motion selectivity correlated with social-network diversity, yielding a significant right pSTS cluster; Fig. S1 and text). Results are clearly from the healthy participant group. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses), and I6 (acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social perception (labeling others’ emotional facial expressions), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 50 healthy adult participants (age 18–29) reported separately and analyzed, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of coordinates and clusters, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group effects, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI examining a social-related process (social sharing/affiliation); (I4) includes a healthy adult sample (female participants aged 20–33) with results reported for the healthy group; (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (second-level random effects, whole-brain corrected findings and whole-brain exploratory results described and tabulated); (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical fMRI work). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults: participants (n=18, ages 19–28) performed a task receiving text messages they believed came from a friend or a computer. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (univariate SPM contrasts, searchlight MVPA and MVCA) with cluster-level correction and coordinates (Table 2, figures). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain evidence suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (25 scanned; ages within 18–65) that uses task-based fMRI during a social economic interaction (repeated public good game) addressing social tie formation (affiliation/attachment and understanding others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM, FSL FEAT) with coordinates and cluster-corrected results, and presents methods, results, and discussion in full. All required inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (mutual understanding) using a task that requires communicative interaction between participants. Participants were healthy adults (54 males, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-level FWE correction) identifying rSTG and other whole-brain contrasts tied to task states; results are described in text, figures, and supplementary materials. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported clearly) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (final N=13, mean age 24.9) using a social interactive joint-attention task (virtual reality gaze-contingent paradigm). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., RJA−RJAc, IJA−IJAc), FDR-corrected statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (abstract states dyadic fMRI during eye-contact social interaction). Inclusion criteria not met/cannot be confirmed: I4 (no participant/sample details to confirm healthy adults 18–65), I5 (no reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps in the provided text), I6 (unable to verify whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement). Exclusion criteria met: none (no evidence this is a non-empirical paper or ROI-only/connectivity-only study from the abstract). Because core information (methods, participants, results) is missing, the study cannot be fully assessed and must be excluded pending full-text availability.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (feeling addressed by gestures and body orientation), satisfying the review objective. It used a task during fMRI (addressment judgments) with healthy adult participants (N=37, ages 20–39). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM8) including main effects and interaction contrasts, with cluster-correction and peak coordinates reported in tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception in healthy adults that meets all inclusion criteria. I3: The task is social-related (perception of person dyads and social interaction congruency) using functional MRI. I4: Sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 21–31 (n=12). I5: The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses and voxelwise contrasts (voxelwise p<.001, cluster-based p<.05) with peak coordinates and tables/figures indicating whole-brain task-evoked maps. I6: Whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an empirical fMRI experiment using a social-related task (perception of emotional crowds and interpersonal dynamics), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=16; ages 19–27), meeting I4. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVAs, cluster-level corrections) with tables of cluster sizes/peak voxels and whole-brain figures, meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion sections (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of deception in strategic social interaction (theory-of-mind, social communication). The sample is healthy adults (n=34, ages 21–32), meeting the age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., simple deception vs. truth; sophisticated deception vs. truth) with Bayesian second-level probability maps and tables of coordinates and figures (Tables 3–8, Figures 2–4), satisfying reporting of whole-brain voxelwise results. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants predicted others' behavior framed as desires or rules (mentalizing/deontic reasoning). Sample: 18 healthy adults aged 18–44, meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, tables of coordinates, conjunction and contrasts) and provides coordinates/tables and figures for results. This is an empirical fMRI study of face-to-face social interaction (eye contact), satisfying the review objective (social processing). Inclusion criteria met: I3 — task is social (dyadic eye contact/interaction); I4 — sample comprises healthy adults (19 pairs, ages 18–33, within 18–65); I5 — the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (GLM group averages, paired t-tests, Z thresholds, cluster tables, MNI coordinates); I6 — whole-brain results are reported and described in text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not only between-group contrasts, not out-of-range ages, and is empirical). The provided document is a theoretical/review article (abstract-only provided) discussing explanations of mirror-touch synesthesia and referencing fMRI evidence, but it does not present original fMRI data, methods, participant samples, or group-level whole-brain activation maps for healthy adults. Exclusion criterion E6 applies (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). This paper reports an fMRI study of social-attribution processing (why/how task) in healthy adults and contains full methods and results. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, interaction contrasts) with cluster-level correction and displays whole-brain results in tables and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy/group-level analysis. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social-affective mimicry task (automatic imitation) directly probing affiliation-relevant social processing (emotion, group membership). Participants are healthy adults (N=41; mean age ~22), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Incongruent>Congruent; Happy vs Angry; Out-group vs In-group) with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and tables of activation coordinates. Whole-brain results are clearly described in methods and results (Tables 2–4 and supplementary material referenced). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study used a social incentive delay task (social reward: smiling faces) and reported task-evoked neural responses. The paper presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation results (FWE-corrected ROI and whole-brain analyses; Tables/Figures report whole-brain contrasts such as reward>neutral and social>monetary, with P values and coordinates), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control cohort. Results are reported in main text, tables and figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references, so fulltext appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 24.6) performing a social gaze-following task (observing eye contact vs. averted gaze), addressing social perception/communication. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 19–31) that explicitly investigates social perception and cognition (ToM, face perception, biological motion, voice perception, language). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, not a non-empirical paper). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of action understanding that probes mentalizing/theory-of-mind processes via why/how questions—an instance of social-related processing (I3). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical study). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30, mean age 24.2) that probes social/emotional processing (gender identification of angry and happy faces vs. neutral shapes). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports fMRI during an interactive social (mentalizing) task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in a sample described as 164 healthy subjects and reports group-level task-associated neural activations across widespread brain regions (i.e., whole-brain activations) and correlations with attachment dimensions. These findings satisfy the review’s social-processing and healthy adult sample requirements and provide whole-brain task-evoked results (reported in text/abstract). However, the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata available), so I could not verify exact participant ages (18–65) or full methodological details that confirm voxelwise unmasked maps. Inclusion is therefore recommended with moderate confidence pending review of the complete article.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of imitation (a social cognitive process related to perception and understanding of others). It reports task-based whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects one-sample t-tests) with reported thresholds, cluster correction, tables/figures and coordinates, and includes healthy adult participants aged 18–25. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study contrasting social vs non-social scenes (satisfies I3). This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social-reputation processing (a social-related task). This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) using task-based fMRI paradigms (EmpaToM, SoVT, False Belief Task) in healthy adult samples (Experiments: N=25, N=65, N=178; ages within 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed a gaze-following task using faces of political (in-group/out-group) personages, addressing social attention and perception of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (incongruent > congruent interference effect), with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level correction, and provides tables/figures of activated clusters and MNI coordinates. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range within 18–65, not non-empirical). This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (social cognition) using a well-established ToM visual paradigm (moving triangles). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R, ToM > Baseline, R > Baseline) with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds and tables/figures of significant clusters (right TPJ, IFG, occipital gyri). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the social-task inclusion criterion (I3). While it uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (HA− > NTR contrast) and meets other sample/map criteria, the experimental paradigm probes negative emotion processing with IAPS images and a simple person-presence button press to ensure attention. The study’s aims and tasks focus on affective/emotion processing and sex differences in fronto-limbic connectivity rather than social-related processes (e.g., affiliation, social communication, explicit perception/understanding of others). Therefore I3 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task contrast), I6 (maps/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates empathy for pain modulated by experimentally induced ingroup/outgroup membership — a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). Sample: 30 healthy adult participants (ages 18–35), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (main effects and interactions) with FWE-corrected maps and cluster/region tables from second-level SPM analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, all male, mean age 23.6) that used a social-related task (viewing violent dyadic interactions with manipulated attentional focus). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., focus on aggressor vs focus on victim; all conditions vs baseline) with statistical maps, tables, and coordinates discussed in the text and figures. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures/tables) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical) apply. This is an fMRI study that explicitly manipulated social vs non-social content during a reading task and tested theory-of-mind/moral-judgment outcomes. Sample: 26 healthy adults aged 19–26 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Social>Non-social; Vivid>Abstract) with tables of peak voxels and cluster sizes, and ROI and mediation analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of implicit social stimulus processing combined with self-referential judgments. It tested 28 healthy adult participants aged 30–50 and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (ANOVA, SPM8) with thresholding (FDR-corrected p<0.05), peak coordinates in MNI space, conjunction and direct contrasts, and figures/tables describing results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports an fMRI task involving social processing (Cyberball social exclusion), uses a healthy adult sample (university students aged within 18–65), and presents group-level whole-brain task contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) with reported coordinates/tables and FWE-corrected results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (racial in-group/out-group face processing with disgust) using a passive viewing task, meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: perception/understanding of others via race/emotion), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages ~21), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses, including a 2×2 ANOVA and interaction contrast with cluster results), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). The provided full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an original task-based fMRI study examining processing of social-content (agency vs. communion) using a valence classification task. Participants were healthy adults (N=42; ages 18–25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (contrasts vs. fixation and implicit baseline), conjunction analyses, and between-condition contrasts with AlphaSim correction; results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. The manuscript includes Introduction, full Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (speech act comprehension: Naming vs Requesting) in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 18–41). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Request>Naming) with FDR-corrected results and tables/figures of activations, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI hyperscanning study using task-based social interaction paradigms (mutual gaze and joint attention), with healthy adult participants (mean ages ~21–23) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (SPM results, tables of coordinates, cluster-level FWE correction). The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing using the Dynamic Social Gestures (DSG) task contrasting social vs nonsocial gestures (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (N=20, mean age 21.41, age range 16.9–25.7) representing an adult sample in the 18–65 range and reported as a single healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FEAT/FLAME, cluster-corrected Z>2.3 p<0.05) with coordinates and tables (Table 1) and figures describing healthy-group effects (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study should be included for the review of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly investigates social-related processing (control of interpersonal trust/distrust) using a task-based paradigm (control-of-trust/distrust). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=60, mean age ~20.25), within 18–65 and reported separately for analyses; thus I4 met. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., trust > age, distrust > age, trust+distrust > age) with FWE correction and whole-brain tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/compassion) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 30.3) using task-based fMRI with naturalistic empathy-evoking film clips; it reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., multisensory vs. unisensory, sad vs. neutral context) with cluster- and FWE-corrections and presents tables/figures of these results. This is an fMRI study of social processing (perceived live vs recorded speech) using a social-interaction task and mentalizing contrasts, meeting I3. This is an empirical fMRI study (N=20 healthy adults, age range 18–27) that used a social cognitive task requiring participants to think about others’ mental states (perception/understanding of others). This is an fMRI study of social learning about others' generosity (social task), with a healthy adult sample (N=30 recruited, N=26 analyzed; ages 19–37), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (cluster-corrected SPM results, tables and figures). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults (n=22 recruited, 21 analyzed; mean age 23.7). This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural processing of empathic vs. unempathic social comments (social communication/understanding of others) in healthy adults. This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (n=21, mean age 24.6) that used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (person perception and person knowledge). This is a task-based fMRI study of theory-of-mind/social processing (social vs non-social story conditions) in healthy adults (N=24, ages within 18–65).
